traits.notes: The seedling displays a whorled arrangement of simple, lanceolate leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. The leaves are shiny and glabrous, with short petioles. The stem is green, smooth, and herbaceous. A pink tag is attached to the stem, likely for identification purposes, and does not affect the morphological assessment. No damage or signs of herbivory are clearly visible on the main leaves. The surrounding litter and log suggest a forest floor environment, but this is not directly relevant to the morphological traits. All images show the same individual from different angles, confirming the whorled leaf arrangement and consistent leaf morphology.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the apex of the stem, forming a whorl)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible across all images)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (narrow, elongated with a pointed tip and broader base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (sharply pointed tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to a narrow base, wedge-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (primary vein runs lengthwise with secondary veins branching off perpendicularly)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are prominent, running parallel to each other and perpendicular to midrib, forming a reticulate pattern)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface is smooth and glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, barely visible in most images, leaves appear sessile or nearly so)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is light to medium green, consistent across images)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no milky or clear sap visible when stem or leaf is damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base or petiole, which would indicate pulvinus)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible)

F. Notes: The seedling displays a whorled arrangement of simple, lanceolate leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. The leaves are shiny and glabrous, with short petioles. The stem is green, smooth, and herbaceous. A pink tag is attached to the stem, likely for identification purposes, and does not affect the morphological assessment. No damage or signs of herbivory are clearly visible on the main leaves. The surrounding litter and log suggest a forest floor environment, but this is not directly relevant to the morphological traits. All images show the same individual from different angles, confirming the whorled leaf arrangement and consistent leaf morphology.
